topicName: Recast Navigation, NavMesh Generation, and Dynamic Obstacles
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Recast Navigation, NavMesh Generation, and Dynamic Obstacles in Unreal Engine"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Unreal Engine uses Recast and Detour as the core backend for its Navigation Mesh (NavMesh) system. This powerful open-source library allows AI controllers to calculate paths efficiently across complex 3D environments. In this tutorial, you will learn how to configure NavMesh generation, handle dynamic obstacles, and optimize performance for real-time applications."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Setting Up the NavMesh Bounds Volume"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"To enable pathfinding in your level, you must define the volume where navigation data is calculated. Unreal Engine does not generate a NavMesh globally by default."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Open your Unreal Engine project and navigate to the Modes panel (or use the Quick Add button)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Search for 'Nav Mesh Bounds Volume' and drag it into your viewport."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scale the volume using the Scale tool (R) to completely encompass the playable walkable areas of your level."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Press the 'P' key on your keyboard to toggle the NavMesh visualization. Walkable surfaces will appear green."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Configuring Recast Navigation Settings"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Recast provides fine-grained control over how the navigation mesh is voxelized and rasterized. You can configure these settings globally via Project Settings."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Go to Edit -> Project Settings -> Engine -> Navigation System."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Expand 'Agents' to view or modify agent radius, height, and maximum step height to match your character dimensions."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"To change Recast-specific voxel sizes, locate the 'RecastNavMesh' actor in your World Outliner or via Project Settings under Navigation Mesh."},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Key properties to tweak in the RecastNavMesh details include:"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cell Size: Controls the voxel resolution along the X and Y axes. Lower values increase accuracy at the cost of higher generation times and memory."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cell Height: Controls the voxel resolution along the Z axis."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Agent Max Slope: Defines the steepest angle a character can walk up."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Handling Dynamic Obstacles"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"In many games, objects move, spawn, or break during gameplay. To prevent AI characters from walking through newly placed obstacles, you must configure your actors to affect the navigation mesh dynamically."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Select the Actor Blueprint that acts as your dynamic obstacle (e.g., a closing door or a moveable crate)."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"In the Details panel, search for the 'Navigation' section."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Check the box for 'Can Affect Navigation'."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Set 'Nav Modifiers' or ensure 'Area Class' is set appropriately (typically to 'NavArea_Obstacle' to block AI)."},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Enabling Dynamic Generation at Runtime"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, static levels generate the NavMesh once upon loading. For dynamic obstacles to update the mesh in real-time, runtime generation must be enabled."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Open Edit -> Project Settings -> Navigation System."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Look for the 'Support Dynamic Generation' property and ensure it is checked."},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"Alternatively, you can configure individual NavMesh volumes to update dynamically using Navigation Invokers for large open-world maps."},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Using Navigation Invokers for Open Worlds"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Generating a NavMesh across an entire massive open world consumes excessive memory and CPU. Navigation Invokers solve this by generating tiles only around specified actors (like the player)."},{"order":31,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Open your Project Settings -> Navigation System and uncheck 'Generate Navigation Only Around Navigation Invokers' if you want a hybrid approach, or check it to strictly rely on invokers."},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Open your Player Character Blueprint."},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click 'Add Component' and search for 'Navigation Invoker'."},{"order":34,"type":"bullet_point","text":"In the component details, adjust the 'Generation Radius' and 'Removal Radius' to define how far ahead the NavMesh should build around the player."},{"order":35,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":36,"type":"paragraph","text":"You have successfully configured Recast Navigation, optimized NavMesh settings, enabled dynamic obstacles, and set up runtime generation using Navigation Invokers. These tools provide a robust foundation for building responsive AI navigation systems in Unreal Engine."}]
